name: Question 9
problem:
Find the general solution of the differential equation

$$
(4x+3{y}^{2}-3{x}^{2}y)\text{d}x+(6xy-{x}^{3})\text{d}y=0.
$$
worked_solution:
Note that the differential equation is of the form

$$
P(x,y)\text{d}x+Q(x,y)\text{d}y=0
$$

where $P(x,y)=4x+3{y}^{2}-3{x}^{2}y$ and $Q(x,y)=6xy-{x}^{3}.$

Let's check if the equation is exact. To do this, we check to see if it passes the exactness test, i.e.,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂y}=\frac{∂Q}{∂x}.
$$

First, let's differentiate $P(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂y}=\frac{∂}{∂y}(4x+3{y}^{2}-3{x}^{2}y)=6y-3{x}^{2}
$$

Now, let's differentiate $Q(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=\frac{∂}{∂x}(6xy-{x}^{3})=6y-3{x}^{2}=\frac{∂P}{∂y}\,✓
$$

So, the given equation is exact and its solution $u(x,y)$ must satisfy the following system:

$$
\frac{∂u}{∂x}=P(x,y),\,\frac{∂u}{∂y}=Q(x,y)
$$

First, we integrate $P(x,y)$ with respect to $x.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(x,y) & =\int P(x,y)\,\text{d}x+f(y) \\  & =\int (4x+3{y}^{2}-3{x}^{2}y)\text{d}x+f(y) \\  & =2{x}^{2}+3x{y}^{2}-{x}^{3}y+f(y)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we integrate $Q(x,y)$ with respect to $y.$  Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(x,y) & =\int Q(x,y)\,\text{d}y+g(x) \\  & =\int (6xy-{x}^{3})\text{d}y+g(x) \\  & =3x{y}^{2}-{x}^{3}y+g(x)\end{aligned}
$$

Comparing the two solutions, we see that we must have

$$
g(x)=2{x}^{2},\,f(y)=0.
$$

Therefore, the general solution $u(x,y)=c$ is

$$
2{x}^{2}+3x{y}^{2}-{x}^{3}y=c.
$$

Question 9
?

Find the general solution of the differential equation

(4x+3y2−3x2y)dx+(6xy−x3)dy=0.

a
x+y2+xy=c
b
2x2+3xy2−x3y=c
c
xy3+x3y+xy=c
d
x3y2−yx=c
e
x2−4xy+y3=c
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Note that the differential equation is of the form

P(x,y)dx+Q(x,y)dy=0

where P(x,y)=4x+3y2−3x2y and Q(x,y)=6xy−x3.

Let's check if the equation is exact. To do this, we check to see if it passes the exactness test, i.e.,

∂P∂y=∂Q∂x.

First, let's differentiate P(x,y) with respect to y:

∂P∂y=∂∂y(4x+3y2−3x2y)=6y−3x2

Now, let's differentiate Q(x,y) with respect to x:

∂Q∂x=∂∂x(6xy−x3)=6y−3x2=∂P∂y✓

So, the given equation is exact and its solution u(x,y) must satisfy the following system:

∂u∂x=P(x,y),∂u∂y=Q(x,y)

First, we integrate P(x,y) with respect to x. Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of y:

u(x,y)=∫P(x,y)dx+f(y)=∫(4x+3y2−3x2y)dx+f(y)=2x2+3xy2−x3y+f(y)

Next, we integrate Q(x,y) with respect to y. Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of x:

u(x,y)=∫Q(x,y)dy+g(x)=∫(6xy−x3)dy+g(x)=3xy2−x3y+g(x)

Comparing the two solutions, we see that we must have

g(x)=2x2,f(y)=0.

Therefore, the general solution u(x,y)=c is

2x2+3xy2−x3y=c.
